header_summary:
Recent Bitcoin Core releases, including versions [31.3](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/release-31.3/) and [30.5](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/release-30.5/), address a medium-severity security vulnerability while providing bug fixes, performance enhancements, and updated translations. The latest security advisory details the vulnerability and mitigation steps at [this link](https://bitcoincore.org/en/2026/11/20/disclose-orphan-inv-stall/), with further technical discussion available via the [mailing list thread](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/c47ceea6-99de-41fe-a97c-928881963eccn@googlegroups.com/T/u). Users on older versions are urged to upgrade for continued security and stability.

Technical improvements in these releases include the implementation of unique transaction inventory processing in the networking layer and optimized continuous integration workflows. Cross-platform compatibility is maintained for Linux, macOS, and Windows, with direct migration support from end-of-life versions and general backward compatibility for wallets. Contributors such as fanquake, Greg Sanders, and willcl-ark are acknowledged, with further details and participation opportunities provided at [Bitcoin Core’s announcements](https://bitcoincore.org/en/list/announcements/join/).

Efforts to formalize secure multisignature wallet setup and PSBT coordination are advancing through open protocols that enhance mutual authentication and eliminate reliance on centralized coordinators. The [KeylayBTC/msp](https://github.com/KeylayBTC/msp) protocol introduces deterministic message identities and robust SAS (Short Authentication String) commitment mechanisms, while inviting peer review on areas such as nonce handling, authentication security, and n-party scalability. These developments aim to address long-standing substitution risks and promote resilient, decentralized multisig operation.

BIP54 introduces new consensus conditions linking block timestamp validity to preceding block values, mitigating adversarial header time hijacking but introducing theoretical attack vectors such as the “slow-sliding-mtp” scenario. These risks are constrained by conservative acceptance windows and practical limitations, preserving network integrity against majority hash rate manipulation [ML thread](https://groups.google.com/g/bitcoindev/c/tKETFYnEtng).

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core security advisory for an easily discoverable vulnerability
recent_posts.summary: - Two new releases fix a medium severity vulnerability and are available for supported major versions.  - A detailed security advisory and accelerated process information are provided through official links.  - Users on version 29.x should upgrade for continued security; further details are available online.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core v30.5 Released
recent_posts.summary: - Bitcoin Core v30.5 provides bug fixes, performance improvements, updated translations, and broad operating system compatibility.  - Upgrade instructions vary by operating system, maintaining backward compatibility with most older wallet versions.  - Technical enhancements include unique transaction processing, CI improvements, and contributions from a collaborative team.

recent_posts.title: Bitcoin Core v31.3 Released
recent_posts.summary: - Bitcoin Core 31.3 delivers bug fixes, performance improvements, and enhanced translations for greater stability.  - Upgrading requires proper shutdown, with specific installation steps for Windows, macOS, and Linux.  - Official support covers recent Linux, macOS, Windows versions, and upgrades from end-of-life releases are supported.

recent_posts.title: PSBT/MuSig2 coordination over Nostr relays: transport invariants for nonce safety under at-least-once delivery
recent_posts.summary: - Identity binding, per-session sequencing, and counter verification are implemented to ensure communication integrity.  - Message identities use a deterministic hash to support duplicate detection and prevent replay attacks.  - The explicit inclusion of the round parameter is being considered to improve robustness after network reconnections.

recent_posts.title: Multisig Session Protocol: draft spec for remote multisig setup and signing needs review
recent_posts.summary: - A new open protocol enables secure, independent multisig wallet key exchanges and authentication.  - Security measures include out-of-band code verification, nonce commitments, and rigorous post-authentication checks.  - Key technical aspects remain under review, including SAS commitment, authentication join, and symmetric key assembly.

recent_posts.title: Open Question on a hypothetical minor "slow-sliding MTP" attack introduced by BIP 54
recent_posts.summary:
- BIP54 adjusts block timestamp validation, introducing new rules and a conservative two-hour acceptance window.
- Adversaries could theoretically exploit header timestamp rules, but attacks require sustained majority hash rate control.
- The protocol's design limits practical exploitation, maintaining security despite possible edge-case vulnerabilities.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` system enhances stale rate observability, assisting in network health diagnostics and quicker issue detection.  - Nodes share stale tip information using feature messages, limiting communication to recent blocks and compressed headers.  - The initiative encourages feedback to optimize node awareness and facilitate improved handling of stale block events.

active_posts.title: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
active_posts.summary: - BIP Editors have actively contributed, processing 596 pull requests and publishing 42 new BIPs.  - Most editorial workload fell on just two editors, with only one active in early 2026.  - A proposal suggests appointing three dedicated editors to ensure effective repository management.

active_posts.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
active_posts.summary: - Several mechanisms are proposed to protect legacy cryptocurrency outputs from quantum-enabled attacks through incentives.  - Quantum Landmines, Staked Auctions, and Sats Auctions introduce collateral penalties and competitive bidding strategies.  - These approaches use cryptography and economic game theory to encourage security and adaptive post-quantum defenses.

active_posts.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts.summary: - The proposal addresses Bitcoin vulnerabilities by recommending improvements for network security and performance.  - Solutions include adjusting timewarp vulnerability, restricting legacy transactions, and invalidating short transactions.  - Some changes, like block size reduction and stricter standardization, have generated debate within the community.

active_posts.title: Unspendable keys in descriptors
active_posts.summary: - Integrating miniscript with taproot introduces challenges in generating practical unspendable keys for wallets.  - Various methods for creating unspendable keys exist, each balancing security, uniqueness, and user experience.  - Further refinement and community discussion are needed to achieve optimal solutions for unspendable key generation.

active_posts.title: Propagation Delay and Mining Centralization: Modeling Stale Rates
active_posts.summary: - Selfish mining leverages block propagation delays to increase miner revenues and encourage centralization.  - Simulation results show that larger pools benefit more from propagation delays, affecting mining fairness.  - Reducing propagation times could improve decentralization and revenue equity among miners of different sizes.

today_in_history_posts.title: Ephemeral Anchors: Fixing V3 Package RBF againstpackage limit pinning
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Greg Sanders proposes "Ephemeral Anchors" to address transaction pinning and enhance smart contract composability.  - The proposal includes watermarking outputs for V3 packages and seeks feedback on complexity and anonymity impacts.  - Open questions remain about MEV risks and SIGHASH_GROUP, while sibling eviction is an alternative solution.

today_in_history_posts.title: Mitigating Channel Jamming with Reputation Credentials: a Protocol Sketch
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Intermediary nodes may tamper with credentials, causing potential value loss for senders.  - Routing nodes typically avoid intentional attacks on paths they benefit from, but accidents remain possible.  - Effective channel jamming protections can minimize deliberate attacks, leaving mainly accidental failures.

today_in_history_posts.title: Propagation Delay and Mining Centralization: Modeling Stale Rates
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Selfish mining strategies can favor larger miners due to block propagation delays and network topology.  - Simulations show that even small differences in propagation times significantly impact revenue and centralization.  - Reducing block propagation delays may improve mining fairness and decrease centralization within the network.
